vendors.name: InvoiceQ
vendors.tagline: Jordanian e-invoicing platform that links existing ERP and accounting systems to the ISTD
vendors.market_position: InvoiceQ says it was founded in 2020 in Jordan as a SaaS company for e-invoicing and integration, and lists an office at King Hussein Business Park in Amman plus a Riyadh office. Its Jordan portal issues and receives e-invoices and connects existing systems (it names Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle, QuickBooks, SAP, Xero and JD Edwards) to the Income and Sales Tax Department's national e-invoicing system. It works as a compliance layer on top of an existing back office rather than replacing it.
pros: Published annual prices in JOD with invoice-volume tiers
Connects existing systems via SOAP, REST APIs or Excel upload
Amman office and Arabic and English interface
Also links to the eFAWATEERcom payment gateway, per InvoiceQ
cons: An e-invoicing layer, not accounting or job-management software
No free tier; the site offers a free consultation, not a trial
Lower plans cap yearly invoice volume (200 or 500)
Full API integration plan is quote-based
vendors.typical_pricing: Basic JOD 120/year (up to 200 invoices); Standard JOD 240/year (up to 500 invoices); Enterprise JOD 500/year (unlimited invoices); ISTD Integration plan with API or internal-system integration is custom-priced. VAT treatment not stated on the pricing page.
vendors.jo_specific_note: InvoiceQ says its platform is compatible with the latest updates from Jordan's Income and Sales Tax Department and offers a custom ISTD Integration plan for firms that want to keep their existing ERP or accounting system. ISTD does not publish a list of approved software, so confirm the integration scope with the vendor.

vendors.name: Mozon
vendors.tagline: Amman-based ERP vendor with a contracting-management module and JoFotara integration
vendors.market_position: Mozon Technologies says it was founded in 2002 and is headquartered in Amman, with a branch in Cairo. It sells an ERP suite, accounting, HR, invoicing and BI software, plus Mozon Contracting Management (MCM) for contracting companies. Mozon says more than 1,500 organizations use its systems.
pros: Contracting module covers budgets, subcontractors and progress invoicing
ERP page lists JoFotara e-invoicing integration, including on POS
Amman head office; Arabic and English software
First-year maintenance and training included, per Mozon
cons: No public prices; quote after a discovery session
ERP implementation takes weeks, per the vendor
Contracting module pricing and scope are only on request
Offices only in Jordan and Egypt
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. Mozon says pricing depends on the scope of work and includes first-year maintenance, training and support.
vendors.jo_specific_note: Mozon's ERP page lists JoFotara e-invoicing integration and pre-built e-invoicing connectors, and its contracting module (MCM) handles progress invoicing and subcontractor records with a direct link to the accounting system. Mozon names Jordanian contractors Ammon Contracting Co. and Zakaria Al-Tarawneh Construction Co. as MCM clients.

vendors.name: Odoo
vendors.tagline: Open-source ERP from Odoo S.A. with a Jordan localization and JoFotara e-invoicing module
vendors.market_position: Odoo is a modular ERP from Odoo S.A. covering accounting, invoicing, projects, inventory, HR and more, sold as a cloud subscription or run from the open-source Community code. Its Jordan localization installs a Jordanian chart of accounts, 16% sales tax and tax report (l10n_jo) plus a JoFotara e-invoicing module (l10n_jo_edi). Implementation is sold separately through Odoo Success Packs or partners.
pros: Jordan chart of accounts, taxes and JoFotara module ship with Odoo
JoFotara module is open source (LGPL-3) in the Community code
One platform for accounting, projects, inventory and HR
Published per-user prices and a free one-app plan
cons: JoFotara needs ISTD credentials (Activity Number, Client ID, Secret Key)
Implementation costs extra via Success Packs or partners
First-year discount on subscriptions; regular prices are higher
Priced in USD, not JOD
vendors.typical_pricing: Published on odoo.com in USD: One App Free $0 (one app, unlimited users); Standard $7.25 per user per month billed yearly or $9.10 billed monthly (first-year discount; regular $8.95 / $11.20); Custom $13.40 per user per month billed yearly or $16.90 monthly (regular $16.40 / $20.90). Implementation, Odoo.sh hosting and in-app services cost extra. Community edition is open source.
vendors.jo_specific_note: Odoo's Jordan localization installs the Jordanian chart of accounts, 16% sales tax, exempt and 0% export taxes and a JoFotara module that sends invoices in UBL 2.1 for real-time validation and puts the JoFotara QR code on the PDF for checking in the Sanad app. You need an Activity Number, Client ID and Secret Key from ISTD, and the company currency must be JOD.

vendors.name: Daftra
vendors.tagline: Cloud accounting and invoicing for Arab-market firms, with a Jordan e-invoice module
vendors.market_position: Daftra is a cloud accounting and business-management system operated by Izam, Inc., according to its terms of service. It covers invoicing, accounting, inventory, CRM and HR, and Daftra says 45K+ businesses use it across 50+ industries. Its Jordan e-invoice product sends invoices directly to the national e-invoicing platform, and it lists a Real Estate & Construction industry profile with project management.
pros: Direct link to Jordan's e-invoicing platform with automatic QR code, per Daftra
Published prices and a 14-day trial with no card required
Accounting, inventory, CRM and HR in one subscription
Jordan phone line and Arabic and English interface
cons: Priced in USD, not JOD
Lower plans cap monthly invoices (100 or 500) and clients
Each plan includes one user; extra users cost $7-9.33 a month
Construction support is an industry profile, not a separate contracting product
vendors.typical_pricing: Basic $30/month, or $240/year ($20/month); Advanced $55/month, or $495/year ($41.25/month); Premium $70/month, or $600/year ($50/month); prices in USD as shown on daftra.com. Each plan includes one user; extra users $7-9.33/month. 14-day free trial, no card required.
vendors.jo_specific_note: Daftra says its Jordan e-invoice product integrates directly with the national e-invoicing platform, adds the required QR code automatically, issues general and specific tax invoices in line with ISTD standards and calculates tax automatically. It offers setup support for the integration and a Jordan sales line.

vendors.name: FawtraPlus
vendors.tagline: Low-cost Jordanian e-invoicing app from Amman software firm JoPython
vendors.market_position: FawtraPlus is a cloud e-invoicing app made by JoPython, an Amman software company founded in 2014. It issues JoFotara e-invoices with QR code, calculates 16% sales tax and adds inventory and tax reports, sold as one annual plan. JoPython says the app is approved by ISTD for the national invoicing system.
pros: Published price: 50 JOD a year for all features
16% sales tax and income-tax invoices with JoFotara QR code
Works offline as a web app and sends invoices by WhatsApp or email
14-day free trial with no card required
cons: Terms say prices may change with prior notice
No project or job-costing features listed on its site
Subscription auto-renews each year unless cancelled
Sales-tax treatment of the 50 JOD price is not stated
vendors.typical_pricing: Published: 50 JOD per year (about 4.17 JOD a month), one plan with all features; auto-renews yearly. 14-day free trial, no card required. Sales-tax treatment of the price not stated.
vendors.jo_specific_note: Built for Jordan: FawtraPlus says it is 100% compatible with JoFotara, adds the QR code and UUID to each invoice, calculates 16% sales tax and supports income-tax invoices for self-employed professionals. It says it is approved by ISTD, though ISTD publishes no list of approved software to check this against.

vendors.name: Fatwarti
vendors.tagline: Amman-based cloud accounting and POS system with JoFotara e-invoicing
vendors.market_position: Fatwarti is an Arabic-language cloud accounting system based in Amman that combines JoFotara e-invoicing, inventory and a point-of-sale module. It covers sales, purchases, expenses, receivables and payables, stock and profit-and-loss reports. Fatwarti says it connects directly to the national invoicing system through the official API.
pros: Direct JoFotara connection via the official API, per Fatwarti
Accounting, inventory and POS in one system
POS supports thermal printers, barcodes and shift management
Free trial with no credit card required
cons: No prices published on the site
Site says one plan has all features but also that POS is advanced-plan only
Arabic-only website; no company legal name or address beyond Amman
No project or job-costing features listed
vendors.typical_pricing: No public prices; the site shows a 'one plan, all features' heading without amounts. Free trial, no credit card required.
vendors.jo_specific_note: Fatwarti says it is 100% compatible with the Income and Sales Tax Department's requirements and sends invoices, including POS sales, directly to JoFotara through the official API. ISTD publishes no list of approved software to check this against.

vendors.name: Stride (Stride Business Solutions)
vendors.tagline: Amman-based Odoo implementation partner
vendors.market_position: STRIDE Business Solutions is an Amman-based firm that implements, customizes and supports Odoo ERP, and sells its own Odoo add-ons for medical labs, pest control and performance management. Odoo's partner directory lists it as a Ready partner in Jordan with 16 customer references, two of them in construction and renovation. It is a services firm, so Odoo subscription costs come on top of its fees.
pros: Local Odoo partner in Amman with Arabic and English support
Listed in Odoo's official partner directory
Implementation, training, migration and ongoing support
Free discovery call
cons: A services firm, not a software product of its own
No public prices
Its site does not mention JoFotara or e-invoicing work
Odoo subscription costs are separate
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices (free discovery call). Odoo subscription costs are separate.
vendors.jo_specific_note: STRIDE is an Amman-based Odoo partner offering support in Arabic and English. Odoo's own Jordan localization includes a JoFotara e-invoicing module, but STRIDE's site does not describe JoFotara setup, so ask whether it will configure the e-invoicing link.

vendors.name: Tax2Gov (T2G)
vendors.tagline: API connector linking existing ERP and POS systems to Jordan's JoFotara
vendors.market_position: Tax2Gov (T2G) is an e-invoicing middleware brand of SB International, Inc., with a head office in Delaware, USA and an office in Tangier, Morocco. It sells API connectors to government e-invoicing platforms across MENA, including a JoFotara connector that links existing ERP and POS systems to Jordan's Income and Sales Tax Department. It does not replace accounting software.
pros: Keeps your existing ERP or POS and adds the JoFotara link
Custom integration work; names SAP, Oracle and Dynamics as examples
Vendor offers AI data validation and 24/7 support
Free consultation
cons: No Jordan office; offices in the US and Morocco
No public prices
Middleware only, not accounting or job-management software
No named ready-made plugin for a specific ERP
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices (free consultation).
vendors.jo_specific_note: Tax2Gov says its universal API connector links ERP and POS systems to ISTD's JoFotara platform and complies with JoFotara phases 1 and 2. It lists no Jordan office and does not claim ISTD approval.

vendors.name: ESKADENIA Software
vendors.tagline: Amman-headquartered software house with a web-based ERP suite
vendors.market_position: ESKADENIA Software was founded in 2000 and is headquartered in Amman, with offices in Dubai and Stockholm and around 300 staff. Its ESKA Business Manager is a web-based ERP covering financials, HR, supply chain, manufacturing, fleet and maintenance, alongside its larger insurance and telecom software lines. ESKADENIA says it holds CMMI Level 5 certification.
pros: Amman headquarters with offices in Dubai and Stockholm
ERP covers finance, HR, supply chain, manufacturing and fleet
Vendor says it holds CMMI Level 5 certification
Company has operated since 2000
cons: No project, contracting or construction module listed
No e-invoicing or JoFotara feature described on its site
No public prices
Aimed at medium-to-large enterprises, per the vendor
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices.
vendors.jo_specific_note: ESKADENIA is headquartered in Amman, but its ERP pages do not describe JoFotara e-invoicing, Jordanian sales tax or project costing. Ask the vendor how it handles JoFotara submission before using it for a contracting business.

vendors.name: Zoho Books
vendors.tagline: Global cloud accounting from Zoho with published USD prices; no Jordan edition or JoFotara link listed
vendors.market_position: Zoho Books is cloud accounting from Zoho covering invoicing, bookkeeping, bank reconciliation and, from the Professional plan, timesheet billing and project profitability. Zoho lists no Jordan edition, so Jordanian firms would use the global version, which Zoho says to evaluate for local compliance before use. Zoho's site names no integration with Jordan's national e-invoicing system (JoFotara).
pros: Published USD prices and a free plan for small revenue
Up to 1,000 invoices a year on the free plan
Timesheet billing and project profitability from the Professional plan
14-day free trial
cons: No Jordan edition; the global version needs a local compliance check
No JoFotara integration named by Zoho
Accounting, not construction management
Priced in USD, not JOD
vendors.typical_pricing: Published in USD on Zoho's global pricing page, per organization per month: billed annually Standard $10 (3 users), Professional $20 (5 users), Premium $30 (10 users), Elite $100 (10 users), Ultimate $200 (15 users); billed monthly $12, $24, $36, $129 and $249. Free plan $0 (1 user plus 1 accountant) while revenue stays under 50K USD a year. Extra users $2.50 a month billed annually ($3 monthly). Prices exclude local taxes; 14-day free trial.
vendors.jo_specific_note: Zoho has no Jordan edition and names no JoFotara integration. If you must issue e-invoices through Jordan's Income and Sales Tax Department system, confirm how you will do it (a separate integration service or ISTD's own tools) before choosing Zoho Books.

vendors.name: QuickBooks
vendors.tagline: Intuit's cloud accounting, sold in Jordan through its global site; JoFotara needs a separate integration
vendors.market_position: QuickBooks Online is cloud accounting software from Intuit. Jordan is served by Intuit's global QuickBooks site, which offers Simple Start, Essentials, Plus and Advanced plans with prices set by location and currency. Intuit's global site names no link to Jordan's national e-invoicing system (JoFotara); InvoiceQ, a Jordanian e-invoicing service, lists QuickBooks among the systems it connects.
pros: Four plans from 1 to 25 users, with accountant access
30-day free trial and no contract
InvoiceQ lists QuickBooks among the systems it connects to JoFotara
cons: No JoFotara link named by Intuit; needs a separate e-invoicing service
No Jordan-specific site or published Jordan price
Accounting, not construction management
Extra cost and setup for the e-invoicing integration
vendors.typical_pricing: Intuit's global site lists Simple Start, Essentials, Plus and Advanced plans, billed monthly with a 30-day free trial and no contract; prices load by visitor location and currency, and no Jordan price could be read on 2026-09-30. Any e-invoicing integration is priced separately by its provider.
vendors.jo_specific_note: Intuit names no Jordan e-invoicing feature in QuickBooks, so firms that must issue JoFotara invoices use a separate service; InvoiceQ lists QuickBooks among the systems it connects to the Income and Sales Tax Department. Check the connector's scope and price before relying on it.

vendors.name: JONEPS
vendors.tagline: Jordan's government e-procurement portal for public tenders, run by GPD and GTD
vendors.market_position: JONEPS (Jordan Online E-Procurement System) is the government portal where public buyers post tender invitations and suppliers register and submit electronic bids, covering works, supplies, services and more. Its footer credits the Government Procurement Department (GPD) and the Government Tenders Department (GTD); GTD runs central works tenders such as water, wastewater, road and building projects. It is a bidding portal, not a lead service.
pros: Official government portal for public tender invitations
Arabic and English interface
Covers works tenders published by the Government Tenders Department
Annual procurement plans published on the portal
cons: Public-sector tenders only
Registration and Sanad activation needed before bidding electronically
Some tenders charge for tender documents
Government-portal interface with no alert service described
vendors.typical_pricing: No registration fee stated on the portal; tender documents can carry a price, paid electronically through JONEPS.
vendors.jo_specific_note: The Government Tenders Department says all Jordanian construction contractors and technical service providers must activate the Sanad service with its e-procurement section to submit bids electronically on JONEPS. GTD also handles contractor classification, so check your classification and Sanad access before a tender closes.

vendors.name: JordanTenders
vendors.tagline: Paid Jordanian tender alerts and contract-award data from Global Tenders Services
vendors.market_position: JordanTenders.com is a paid tender-information service that says it is part of Global Tenders Services Pvt. Ltd. (GTS), a global procurement facilitator. It offers searchable Jordanian tenders from government departments, local authorities and public and private entities, with a Construction and Real Estate category, daily email alerts and, on higher plans, contract-award data. It is an alert and search layer, not the official bidding portal.
pros: Published annual prices, from $295 USD
Daily email alerts and unlimited keyword search
Construction and Real Estate sector category
Free sample tenders by email
cons: Government tender invitations are also posted on the official JONEPS portal
Contract awards not included in Basic
Priced in USD
No operator address published on the site
vendors.typical_pricing: Basic $295 USD, Premium $395 USD, Platinum $495 USD, each for 12 months (1, 3 and 5 accounts); contract awards from Premium, dedicated account manager on Platinum.
vendors.jo_specific_note: JordanTenders emails daily Jordanian tender alerts, including construction and real estate. Public tender invitations are also posted on the official JONEPS portal, so weigh the $295-$495 yearly fee against checking JONEPS yourself; the extra value is alerts, search, private-sector tenders and, from Premium, contract awards.

vendors.name: JOFICO (Jordan French Insurance)
vendors.tagline: Jordanian multi-line insurer founded in 1976, with a nine-policy engineering line
vendors.market_position: Jordan French Insurance Company (JOFICO) says it was founded in 1976 in cooperation with Compagnie Financière du Groupe Victoire. It is listed on the Amman Stock Exchange (JOFR) and sells motor, health, travel, home, fire, liability, marine, engineering, aviation and credit insurance. Saraya News reported in February 2026 that JOFICO signed a memorandum of understanding to study a possible merger with Gulf Insurance Group; no outcome had been announced on JOFICO's site by September 2026.
pros: Engineering page lists Contractors All Risks and Construction Plant and Machinery
Also lists Erection All Risks and Decennial Liability policies
Operating since 1976
Listed on the Amman Stock Exchange (JOFR)
cons: Website in Arabic only
No prices published; cover is quoted
Possible merger with Gulf Insurance Group under study
No online quote form found on the engineering page
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. Contact JOFICO by phone or through an agent or broker.
vendors.jo_specific_note: JOFICO's Arabic engineering page lists Contractors All Risks, Construction Plant and Machinery, Machinery Breakdown, Erection All Risks, Electronic Equipment and Decennial Liability policies, among others. Check the status of its reported merger talks with Gulf Insurance Group before a long-term placement.

vendors.name: gig Jordan (Arab Orient)
vendors.tagline: Jordanian arm of Kuwait-based Gulf Insurance Group, majority-owned by Fairfax, with an English engineering line
vendors.market_position: GIG Jordan says it was founded in 1996 as Arab Orient Insurance Company and joined Kuwait-based Gulf Insurance Group (GIG) in 2009. Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings became GIG's largest shareholder in 2023 and later raised its stake to 97%, according to GIG Jordan. It is listed on the Amman Stock Exchange (GIGJ) and says AM Best rates it A-.
pros: English engineering page lists Contractors' All Risks and Plant and Machinery
Online quote-request form for each engineering policy
Also sells professional indemnity and employers liability
Part of Gulf Insurance Group; AM Best A- rating, per GIG Jordan
cons: No prices published; cover is quoted
No erection all risks or decennial policy listed on the engineering page
Quote request is a form, not an instant online price
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. GIG Jordan takes quote requests through an online form on its site.
vendors.jo_specific_note: GIG Jordan's engineering page lists Contractors' All Risks, Contractors' Plant and Machinery, Machinery Breakdown, Electronic Equipment, Deterioration of Stock and Boiler cover, and its general lines include professional indemnity and employers liability. Each engineering policy has an online quote-request form.

vendors.name: Jordan Insurance Company (JIC)
vendors.tagline: Amman insurer established in 1951, rated B (Fair) by AM Best
vendors.market_position: Jordan Insurance Company (JIC) is an Amman-based life and non-life insurer, established in March 1951 according to its Amman Stock Exchange profile, and listed on the ASE (JOIN). AM Best says it consistently ranks in the top three in Jordan by gross written premium, with revenue concentrated in motor and medical business. In July 2026 AM Best affirmed its financial strength rating at B (Fair) with a stable outlook.
pros: Operating since 1951
AM Best says it ranks in the top three in Jordan by premium
Life and non-life lines under one insurer
Listed on the Amman Stock Exchange (JOIN)
cons: AM Best financial strength rating B (Fair)
AM Best notes non-life technical losses, particularly in motor
Website product pages could not be read; confirm engineering cover directly
No prices published; cover is quoted
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. Contact JIC or a broker for a quote.
vendors.jo_specific_note: AM Best describes JIC as holding an established position in Jordan's insurance market, but JIC's website did not show its engineering products when checked, so ask JIC or your broker directly whether it writes Contractors All Risks and plant cover for your project.

vendors.name: Middle East Insurance Company (MEICO)
vendors.tagline: Jordanian multi-line insurer since 1962 with a full engineering line; stopped writing motor in 2026
vendors.market_position: Middle East Insurance Company (MEICO) says it has operated in Jordan since 1962 and is a public shareholding company listed on the Amman Stock Exchange (MEIN). It sells property, engineering, liability, marine, aviation, financial lines, group medical and life cover. MEICO discontinued its motor insurance license effective 1 January 2026 with Central Bank of Jordan approval, and says existing motor policies are serviced until they expire.
pros: Engineering page lists Contractors' All Risks and Erection All Risks
Contractor's Plant and Machinery and Machinery Breakdown cover
Online quote form for engineering policies
Operating since 1962; listed on the Amman Stock Exchange (MEIN)
cons: No longer sells motor insurance, so site vehicles need another insurer
No prices published; cover is quoted
No decennial liability policy listed on the engineering page
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. MEICO takes quote requests through a form on its website or its contact page.
vendors.jo_specific_note: MEICO's English engineering page lists Contractors' All Risks, Erection All Risks, Contractor's Plant and Machinery, Machinery Breakdown with loss of profit, Electronic Equipment and Deterioration of Stock cover. It gave up its motor license from 1 January 2026, so insure company vehicles elsewhere.

vendors.name: ZenHR
vendors.tagline: Bilingual cloud HR and payroll with Jordan SSC and end-of-service calculations
vendors.market_position: ZenHR is a cloud HR and payroll platform for the Middle East and North Africa; it says it is localized for 11 MENA countries and serves clients from five offices in the region, including a Jordan phone line. Its Jordan page says the product is '100% compliant with Jordan Labor Law & SSC' and names customers in Amman, Irbid and Zarqa. Beyond payroll it covers attendance, employee self-service, performance and applicant tracking.
pros: Its Jordan page states SSC contribution and Labor Law calculations
Automates Jordanian end-of-service pay by contract type, duration and reason
Bilingual Arabic and English web and mobile apps
Payroll exports to QuickBooks, Xero, SAP, NetSuite, Dynamics 365 and Odoo
Bank salary transfer files in bank-required formats
cons: No public prices; quotes depend on headcount, countries and bundle
Demo and quote first; no free trial mentioned on the pricing page
A full HR suite may be more than a small contractor needs for payroll only
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. ZenHR says pricing is quoted per organization based on headcount, countries of operation and bundle (Value or Advanced).
vendors.jo_specific_note: ZenHR's Jordan page says it is '100% compliant with Jordan Labor Law & SSC' and automates salary, deduction and SSC contribution calculations as well as Jordanian end-of-service benefits. It lists a Jordan phone number alongside its Saudi and UAE lines, and payroll can be run in Arabic or English.

vendors.name: MenaITech / MenaPAY
vendors.tagline: Regional HR and payroll suite with an Amman office
vendors.market_position: Menaitech sells HR, payroll, attendance and self-service software across the Middle East, with its main office in Riyadh and further offices in Amman, Jeddah, New Cairo, Dubai and Kuwait City. It says it has worked in HR technology for over 20 years and has 'nearly 2,000 trusted clients'. MenaPAY is its payroll product, alongside CURIO for HR and talent management, MenaTA for time and attendance and MenaME for employee self-service.
pros: Amman office and a dedicated Jordan country site
Full HR suite: payroll, HR, attendance, self-service and analytics
End-of-service, provident fund and retroactive pay calculations
Vendor-run MenaPAY certification courses for payroll staff
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified, per Menaitech
cons: No public prices; demo request only
The MenaPAY page names Saudi social insurance rules, not Jordan's SSC
Main office is in Riyadh, not Amman
A full HR suite may be more than a small contractor needs
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices (demo request).
vendors.jo_specific_note: Menaitech has an Amman office and runs its Jordan site at menaitech.com/en/. The MenaPAY page describes 'pre-loaded country compliance profiles' but spells out only Saudi social insurance and wage protection, so ask in the demo how it handles Jordan SSC contributions and income tax.

vendors.name: Yomly (formerly EmiratesHR)
vendors.tagline: Dubai-based cloud HR and payroll with a Jordan payroll page
vendors.market_position: Yomly is a cloud HR and payroll platform run from Dubai Media City by SevenHR Information Technology Consultants LLC; it says it was established in 2018 as EmiratesHR. Yomly says it has '250+ Happy Clients' in more than 50 countries across MENA and Southeast Asia. Its Jordan page says the payroll system is 'designed to align with local labor laws and tax regulations in Jordan'.
pros: Jordan page states alignment with Jordan labor and tax rules and automated deductions
Multi-country, multi-currency payroll
Gratuity and end-of-service tracking and bank salary files
Arabic and English interfaces with Android and iOS apps
cons: Based in the UAE with no Jordan office listed
The Jordan page does not mention SSC or social security
No public prices; demo first
Aimed at larger employers, which may be more than a small trades firm needs
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices (book a demo).
vendors.jo_specific_note: Yomly's Jordan page says its payroll is 'designed to align with local labor laws and tax regulations in Jordan' and automates salary calculations, deductions and benefits, but it does not mention Social Security Corporation contributions, so confirm the SSC handling in a demo.

vendors.name: GTS One ERP
vendors.tagline: Amman-based Arabic HRMS and payroll within a wider ERP suite
vendors.market_position: GTS Software sells GTS One, a suite of ERP, HR and payroll, CRM, point of sale, fixed asset and property management software, from an office in Jabal Al Hussein, Amman, with further offices in Ramallah and Hebron. Its HRMS is described as an Arabic HR system available in the cloud or as SaaS, covering payroll, attendance, leave, loans, self-service and recruitment. Payroll posts ledger entries to the general ledger, which suits firms that also want the ERP.
pros: Local vendor with an office in Amman
Payroll links to biometric attendance devices and auto-generated timesheets
Bank direct deposit to multiple bank accounts, plus WPS support
Multiple trial payroll runs before the final run
Payroll ledger posting to the general ledger in its ERP
cons: Its site does not mention Jordan SSC or income tax handling
No public prices
Its own pages give conflicting company history and customer figures
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices.
vendors.jo_specific_note: GTS is based in Amman and describes an Arabic HR and payroll system, but its payroll pages list generic features (trial runs, bank deposit, WPS) without naming Social Security Corporation contributions or Jordan income tax, so confirm both before relying on it for Jordan payroll.

vendors.name: Jordan Construction Contractors Association (JCCA)
vendors.tagline: Statutory contractors' association: registration is required to practise contracting
vendors.market_position: The Jordanian Construction Contractors Association is the statutory body for contractors under Construction Contractors Law No. 13 of 1987, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2014, with its main office in Amman. The law requires a contractor to be licensed, register with the Ministry of Industry and Trade and with the Association, and be classified within a temporary licence period of up to one year. The Government Tenders Department says it manages contractor licensing and classification and publishes the Contractor Classification Instructions of 2020.
pros: Registration is the legal basis for practising contracting in Jordan
Registered, classified contractors can sign works contracts with ministries, municipalities and companies
Clear statute, published in English by the Association
Classification forms and instructions are published by the Government Tenders Department
cons: Several steps: licence, trade registration, Association registration and classification
Active membership is limited to Jordanian contractors; foreign contractors register as non-active members
Practising without registration carries fines of JD 1,000-5,000, doubled for a repeat
No public fee schedule was found
vendors.typical_pricing: Registration fee plus annual subscription, set under the Association's rules; no public fee schedule was found.
vendors.jo_specific_note: Under Article 8 of the Construction Contractors Law, no one may practise contracting in Jordan without prior registration with the Association and payment of its fees, and no ministry, municipality, public shareholding company or other entity may sign a works contract with a contractor who is not registered and classified with the Association; such a contract is void. A new contractor's licence is temporary, for up to one year, during which the contractor must be classified.

vendors.name: Jordan Engineers Association (JEA)
vendors.tagline: Statutory engineers' association: registration is required to practise engineering
vendors.market_position: The Jordan Engineers Association regulates the engineering profession in Jordan under the Engineers Association Law (No. 15 of 1972, as amended). It began as a society of engineers in 1948 and its first law was issued in 1972; its website shows 192,275 registered engineers and 1,332 registered engineering consulting offices and companies. It also runs health insurance, retirement and social solidarity funds and a training academy for members.
pros: Registration is the legal basis for practising engineering in Jordan
Registered engineers and engineering offices can sign and certify drawings
Published registration conditions and fees
Member health insurance, retirement and social solidarity funds
cons: Practising without registration can bring fines of 200 to 1,000 dinars, doubled for a repeat
Separate registration conditions and documents for foreign engineers and graduates of foreign universities
Annual subscription must be kept paid
Foreign engineering offices must work with a Jordanian engineering office
vendors.typical_pricing: Graduates of Jordanian universities pay JD 136 on application (JD 75 application review fee and JD 61 annual subscription fees), per JEA's registration conditions; other applicant groups have separate conditions, and engineering office registration is separate.
vendors.jo_specific_note: Under the Engineers Association Law, engineering studies and designs may be prepared only by engineering offices and companies registered with the Association, and building work may be carried out only under drawings signed by registered engineers and certified by the Association. Government bodies, municipalities and other institutions must check that an engineer or engineering office is registered before hiring or contracting with them.

vendors.name: Companies Control Department (CCD)
vendors.tagline: Jordan's company registrar under the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply
vendors.market_position: The Companies Control Department registers and supervises companies in Jordan under Companies Law No. 22 of 1997 and its amendments, and sits under the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply. It registers limited liability, partnership, shareholding, exempt, civil, non-profit and foreign companies, handles amendments, financial statements and liquidations, and keeps a beneficial owner registry. Registration is filed online through its e-services portal.
pros: Online registration; an LLC can be registered within 24 hours when no prior approvals are needed
An LLC can be formed by a single partner
Published service cards with fees and required documents
Online company search by name, partner or registration number
cons: Some business purposes need prior approvals, for example from the Ministry of Public Works or Ministry of Interior
Ongoing duties such as filing financial statements and beneficial owner records
Service guides are mostly in Arabic
Fees rise with capital
vendors.typical_pricing: LLC registration, per CCD's service card: a registration fee based on capital (minimum JD 250), JD 10 document deposit, JD 15 publication fee and JD 10 power-of-attorney deposit, plus stamp duty on capital; other company types have their own service cards.
vendors.jo_specific_note: Under the Construction Contractors Law, a contractor first obtains a contracting licence, then registers the company with the Ministry of Industry and Trade (through this department) and with the Jordanian Construction Contractors Association, and must then be classified. CCD's LLC service card lists Ministry of Public Works approval among the possible prior approvals.

vendors.name: Income and Sales Tax Department (ISTD)
vendors.tagline: Jordan's tax authority: income tax, 16% general sales tax and the JoFotara e-invoicing system
vendors.market_position: The Income and Sales Tax Department, under the Ministry of Finance, administers Income Tax Law No. 34 of 2014 and General Sales Tax Law No. 6 of 1994; it was formed by merging the income tax and sales tax departments on 16 August 2004. It handles tax registration, returns and payments, which can be paid through eFawateercom, and says it offered 70 e-services in 2025. It also runs JoFotara, the national electronic invoicing system.
pros: Registration, returns and payments can be handled online
JoFotara registration and invoicing through a web portal or the Fawatiri app
Tax bills can be paid through eFawateercom
Published laws, rate schedules and FAQs
cons: General sales tax registration becomes mandatory once sales pass thresholds that differ for goods and services
Invoices must be issued through JoFotara or software linked to it, which may need new invoicing software
Late sales tax payment is fined four per thousand of the tax due for each week of delay, per ISTD's sales tax FAQ
Most guidance documents are in Arabic
vendors.typical_pricing: Government authority: general sales tax is 16% under Law No. 6 of 1994, with reduced, zero and exempt rates for listed goods and services; income tax at the statutory rates. No registration fee is shown on the ISTD pages read.
vendors.jo_specific_note: ISTD's invoicing regulation, as amended in 2023, recognises electronic invoices issued through the national JoFotara system or through software linked to it, and Jordanian press reported that use of the system became mandatory from the start of April 2025. Contractors issuing invoices should confirm that their accounting software is linked to JoFotara.

vendors.name: Social Security Corporation (SSC)
vendors.tagline: Jordan's state social insurance fund for employers and workers
vendors.market_position: The Social Security Corporation runs Jordan's statutory social insurance scheme under the Social Security Law, funded by employer and employee contributions on insured wages. Its insurances include old-age, disability and death pensions and work-injury cover. An amended Social Security Law, centred on retirement rules, passed the House of Representatives in June 2026, according to Petra.
pros: Statutory social insurance for workers, funded jointly by employer and employee
Covers old-age, disability and death pensions and work injuries
Contributions are a fixed share of insured wages, so payroll costs are predictable
cons: The employer share of 14.25% of insured wages is a recurring cost on top of pay
Retirement rules were being amended in 2026; check the current rules with the SSC
Rates here come from PwC's tax summary; confirm current rates and registration steps with the SSC
vendors.typical_pricing: No fee schedule read. Contributions, per PwC's Jordan tax summary (reviewed July 2026): 14.25% of insured wages paid by the employer and 7.5% by the employee.
vendors.jo_specific_note: Employers in Jordan pay social security contributions for their workers to the Social Security Corporation: 14.25% from the employer and 7.5% from the employee, according to PwC's tax summary. Payroll software sold in Jordan should calculate these contributions; ask the vendor to confirm how it handles SSC.
